title: OOP Basics
intro: Learn the basic ideas of OOP Basics in simple English. Read the explanation and example first; the quiz asks only from the concepts taught here.

items.heading: Class
items.text: A class is a blueprint that defines the data and behavior an object can have.

items.heading: Object
items.text: An object is an instance created from a class.

items.heading: __init__
items.text: __init__ is commonly used to initialize an object’s attributes when it is created.

items.heading: self
items.text: self refers to the current object instance inside an instance method.

items.heading: Attribute
items.text: An attribute is data stored on an object or associated with a class.

items.heading: Method
items.text: A method is a function defined inside a class and used through an object or class.

items.heading: Creating objects
items.text: Calling a class such as Car() creates an object instance.

items.heading: Encapsulation
items.text: Encapsulation means keeping related data and behavior together and controlling how internal details are accessed.

items.heading: Inheritance
items.text: Inheritance lets one class reuse or extend behavior from another class.

items.heading: Polymorphism
items.text: Polymorphism lets different objects be used through a common operation or interface.

items.heading: Class design
items.text: Small, focused classes are usually easier to understand, test and maintain.
